key_insight: A fault-tolerant bosonic sensing protocol preserves Heisenberg-limited displacement sensitivity for longer by protecting the accumulated signal in an error-corrected qubit register.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a route to noise-resilient bosonic sensors using controlled displacements, repetition-encoded qubits, and repeated parity measurements and resets.
method: Construct an optimal error-correcting code under a mean photon-number constraint.
Transfer the displacement signal into a repetition-encoded qubit register via controlled displacements.
Repeatedly measure boson parity and reset the probe to remove noise while preserving the stored logical phase.
evidence_signal: Theoretical analysis gives logical failure suppression of order p^((d+1)/2) and Fisher information scaling as NT² for sensing times of order γ_A^(-(d+1)/2), versus O(γ_A^(-1)) without fault tolerance.
watch_item: The stated scaling requires sufficiently small residual signals and the analyzed noise model; practical gains depend on reliable control, parity measurements, and resets.
paper_title: Fault-Tolerant Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Metrology with Bosonic Probes
